issue.title: Extracting frames for prediction
issue.body:
Hi,

I am trying to use your pretrained model for predicting actions on the recordings you provide in Google Drive.
I downloaded the recordings and generated fine grained labels using [gen_fine_labels.py](https://github.com/assembly-101/assembly101-action-recognition/blob/main/gen_fine_labels.py), as you described.
When I run test_models.py, a `FileNotFoundError` is raised: It seems the dataloader is looking for frames, e.g., `nusar-2021_action_both_9011-a01_9011_user_id_2021-02-01_153724/C10095_rgb/C10095_rgb_0000000147.jpg`.

I tried creating these frames using the utilities from TSM (vid2img_kinetics.py, vid2img_sthv2.py), but they create frames with a mismatching file name (e.g., `img_16712.jpg`).
How can I fix this issue? Should I change the utilities of TSM, to produce the expected file names? Or am I missing a folder on Google Drive, that has the needed frames?

Thank you very much for your help with this issue!

2. Construct the TSM model without shifting operation and load your pre-trained weights.
3. Replace the last dropout layer `with nn.Idnetity()` [as mentioned](https://github.com/assembly-101/assembly101-action-recognition/issues/11#issuecomment-1799142172): `setattr(model.base_model, model.base_model.last_layer_name, nn.Identity())`
4. Process input images through [your modified transformer](https://github.com/assembly-101/assembly101-action-recognition/issues/6#issuecomment-1578041681).
5. Compute the L2 distance between the extracted and the provided features using `np.linalg.norm()`.

## Background
I'd like to ensure my feature extraction code is correct. I ran it using your pre-trained TSM and compared the extracted features with yours provided in the Google drive. If the both are same, it means that the code is correct. Then, I can use it to extract features from other datasets. The situation is similar to #6.

issue.title: Feature Extraction
issue.body:
Hi! 

I'm trying to extract the features of a dataset after training the proposed TSM on it. Following the suggestion in the issue https://github.com/assembly-101/assembly101-action-recognition/issues/1, I should train the 2D backbone without shift, and this is what I'm trying:

`python main.py dataset RGB --arch resnet50 --num_segments 8 --gd 20 --lr 0.001 --lr_steps 20 40 --epochs 50 --batch-size 32 -j 16 --dropout 0.5 --consensus_type=avg --eval-freq=1 --npb --tune_from=pretrained_models/tsm_rgb_epic.ckpt --gpus 0 1
`
In this way the features in output of the base_model have a shape of (128, 2048). This is due to the number of segments, 128 = num_segments*batch_size. 

How should I handle this problem to save the correct 2048-D tensor per frame?

Kind regards,
Alessandro

_Originally posted by @aleflabo in https://github.com/assembly-101/assembly101-action-recognition/issues/1#issuecomment-1791697133_

comments.body:
Hi Alessandro,

The TSM is trained using the usual 8/16-frame input strategy (with temporal shifts) on Assembly101. We only extract the per-frame TSM features using the 2D backbone of the pretrained TSM (from the first sentence), without any shifting operation.

Please feel free to reply to this if you have any further queries.

Best,
Dibyadip

Got it, thank you! 

Kind regards,
Alessandro

Hi Dibyadip,

I've followed your suggestions and extracted the features after the 2D backbone. Precisely, the features are saved after the forward of the base_model (at this line: https://github.com/assembly-101/assembly101-action-recognition/blob/00d3c3bb3af75ce38ae406614a7cb034aecdebc0/TSM-action-recognition/ops/models.py#L272). 

All the features saved have the same indexes with the value 0. Here is an example of the first 20 features (out of 2048) of a frame and the zeros in different positions can be seen. 
```
array([0.        , 0.00726067, 0.06628822, 0.        , 0.01285915,
       0.01205407, 0.00071825, 0.23438536, 0.        , 0.        ,
       0.        , 0.00035547, 0.00821526, 0.        , 0.        ,
       0.        , 0.        , 0.02248539, 0.06791941, 0.        ],
      dtype=float32)
```

I think this is happening cause the shifting is not enabled. Do you have any advice on how to handle this problem?
The train is done using the command I posted in the first comment. 

Thanks,
Alessandro

The last layer of the base_model is a Dropout layer and that seems to be causing the zeros in the output. 
Should I just replace it with an Identity layer?

The last two layers of the base_model are: 
```
(avgpool): AdaptiveAvgPool2d(output_size=1)
(fc): Dropout(p=0.8, inplace=False)
```

Looking at the code of RULSTM 
(https://github.com/fpv-iplab/rulstm/blob/e648c7ee40a1a71381bfaa7563f2e8a6935275ab/FEATEXT/extract_example_rgb.py#L22C9-L22C9
), they replace the last two layers. Should I do the same?


Thanks,
Alessandro

Hi Alessandro, 

Yes, as mentioned in issue #6, we follow RU-LSTM extraction code by just replacing TSN with TSM and also changing the input transforms. This means replacing the dropout layer with `nn.Identity()` i.e. `model.base_model.fc = nn.Identity()`

Please feel free to open this issue if you have any further queries.

Best,
Dibyadip

issue.title: Pretrained model evaluation
issue.body:
Hi and thanks for the dataset.

I'm running the evaluation code with the pre-trained model provided, however just utilising data from view v-2. 

On the validation data the model achieves an Overall Prec@1 = 38.84, which does not match the value of 40.6 provided in table 6 of your paper.

I just wanted to check if the values within table 6 calculated from the test set which we can not access? or if there is a problem with my decoded frames/data set pipeline?

Cheers, Matthew.

comments.body:
Hi,

The results provided in Table 6 of our main paper are indeed evaluated on the test set. We have observed a trend in the accuracy on the full test set (for TSM) being generally around 1% higher than the validation set.

We withhold the ground truth action labels for the test split. However, you can generate (verb/object/action) accuracy for the test set  by submitting your prediction `.json` file to our [codalab platform](https://codalab.lisn.upsaclay.fr/competitions/5256).

Best,
Assembly101 Team

issue.title: TSM Feature extraction
issue.body: HI! I've trained TSM with a subset of the videos and I'm trying to extract features to have features similar to what you provide. Some advice?

comments.body:
Hi Camillo,

You may find some information in this [issue](https://github.com/assembly-101/assembly101-action-recognition/issues/1).
We modify the [RU-LSTM](https://github.com/fpv-iplab/rulstm/blob/master/FEATEXT/extract_example_rgb.py) code for feature extraction by replacing the TSN with a TSM.

Please let us know if you face any issues.

Using your pretrained model [(link)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/11uFkqg1tWfWeATukjFL_HXHB6Gs1iGfU/view), I am unable to obtain the same extracted features as yours. I want to obtain the features that you have extracted in order to validate the code and use it to extract features using my trained model. Any suggestions?

Hi Camillo,

Can you explain what do you mean by "unable to obtain the same extracted features" i.e. how do you measure it? Are you comparing with some of our benchmarks?

**Note**: This pretrained [TSM model](https://drive.google.com/file/d/11uFkqg1tWfWeATukjFL_HXHB6Gs1iGfU/view) has been trained on fixed+ego (all 12 views).

I have downloaded the TSM features provided by you, and I want to obtain the same features (using your pretrained model) to ensure that the extraction code is correct. Then, I will proceed with the extraction using the model trained by myself.

Hi Camillo,

If I understood correctly, are you using your custom per-frame feature extraction code using our pretrained (on all 12 views) TSM and then comparing with the per-frame features provided by us in the drive?

What metric are you using to calculate the feature similarity? (e.g. L2, L1?) Note that the features might will not be exact and will depend on the input transform you are using and the best way to check is to run any [segmentation baselines](https://github.com/assembly-101/assembly101-temporal-action-segmentation) with your features and see if you can reproduce the results.

Instead of using the [RU-LSTM](https://github.com/fpv-iplab/rulstm/blob/master/FEATEXT/extract_example_rgb.py#L27) transforms, please use the image transforms provided in [test_models.py](https://github.com/assembly-101/assembly101-action-recognition/blob/main/TSM-action-recognition/test_models.py#L155) as follows:
```python
transform = torchvision.transforms.Compose([
            GroupScale(net.scale_size),
            GroupCenterCrop(input_size),
            Stack(roll=(this_arch in ['BNInception', 'InceptionV3'])),
            ToTorchFormatTensor(div=(this_arch not in ['BNInception', 'InceptionV3'])),
            GroupNormalize(net.input_mean, net.input_std),
        ])
```

Let me know if this works !

issue.title: Missing hand poses and hand poses with start_f & end_f out of range in test_challenge.csv
issue.body:
Hi! Thanks for your great work.

There are 21900 samples in `test_challenge.csv` provided in [fine-grained-annotations](https://github.com/assembly-101/assembly101-annotations/blob/main/fine-grained-annotations). When I preprocessed them and convert 30 fps to 60 fps, I found the number of the valid samples is not 21900, but 20882.

I have figured out why those **21900-20882=1018** samples are invalid:
1. In function `gather_split_annotations()` in [this script](https://github.com/assembly-101/assembly101-action-recognition/blob/main/MS-G3D-action-recognition/Preprocess/1_generate_pose_data.py), **286 samples** are ignored since they can not be found in `jsons_list_poses`. I printed the names of those missing samples. They should have been read from a json file named `'nusar-2021_action_both_9025-c12a_9025_user_id_2021-02-18_111731.json'`. But the [Google Drive](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1tQbqbXdGfU40kBKfXN4TpKru0s5O4LIa) doesn't provide this json file.
2. To convert 30 fps to 60 fps, I wrote the following lines in preprocessing script:
```
curr_data['start_frame'] = aData.start_frame * 2 + 1        # 30 fps -> 60 fps
curr_data['end_frame'] = aData.end_frame * 2 + 1            # 30 fps -> 60 fps
```
In `main()` function of the [script](https://github.com/assembly-101/assembly101-action-recognition/blob/main/MS-G3D-action-recognition/Preprocess/1_generate_pose_data.py), the `start_f` & `end_f` are calculated using the following lines:
```
start_f = max(0, segment['start_frame'] - contex_val) # Adjust start_frame with context
end_f = min(segment['end_frame'] + contex_val + 1, len(hand_labels)) # Adjust end_frame with context
```
where `hand_labels` are also 60 fps.
Most samples are handled correctly, but surprisingly, **732 samples** get `start_f` & `end_f` which are out of range. `segment['start_frame'] - contex_val` and `segment['end_frame'] + contex_val + 1` are both bigger than `len(hand_labels)`, resulting in a strange situation where `start_f>end_f=len(hand_labels)`.
```
epic_joints_seg = [] # Stores all handposes frame by frame for current segment
start_f = max(0, segment['start_frame'] - contex_val) # Adjust start_frame with context
end_f = min(segment['end_frame'] + contex_val + 1, len(hand_labels)) # Adjust end_frame with context
for img_index in range(start_f, end_f, 1):     # This loop is ignored because start_f>end_f=len(hand_labels)
    ......
    epic_joints_seg.append(landmarks3d)        # So the epic_joints_seg list will be empty
```
In this case, epic_joints_seg will be empty, so these **732 samples** are also invalid.


These 1018 invlid test samples (5% of the test set) has no pose data. They will definitely fail to predict. It may cause lower accuracy reports in your CodaLab Challenge Page, if all 21900 samples in `test_challenge.csv` are computed. I don't know if this is okay.
Thanks for your help in advance.

Best,
Necca

issue.title: Feature extraction with pre-trained TSM
issue.body:
Hi!

I had a question concerning the TSM pre-extracted features. Since the TSM network requires 8 segments to perform shifting, which frames do you sample during the per-frame feature extraction? 
Thank you for your answer in advance and I look forward to hearing from you!

Best,
Olga

comments.body:
Hi!

If you are asking about the per-frame TSM features for action anticipation/segmentation, we directly use the 2D backbone of the TSM (without any shifting operations) pretrained for action recognition to extract the features for each frame.
We also tried a (2D backbone + shifting) version where we densely sampled 8 consecutive frames in a sliding window manner and have the 2048-D segment feature correspond to the middle frame of the segment - but the performance improvement was extremely marginal. Hence, we sticked to the lightweight 2D backbone only.

Hi!

Thank you for the response, that's exactly what I meant :)

Best,
Olga

Hi! 

I'm trying to extract the features of a dataset after training the proposed TSM on it. Following the suggestion above, I should train the 2D backbone without shift, and this is what I'm trying:

`python main.py dataset RGB --arch resnet50 --num_segments 8 --gd 20 --lr 0.001 --lr_steps 20 40 --epochs 50 --batch-size 32 -j 16 --dropout 0.5 --consensus_type=avg --eval-freq=1 --npb --tune_from=pretrained_models/tsm_rgb_epic.ckpt --gpus 0 1
`
In this way the features in output of the base_model have a shape of (128, 2048). This is due to the number of segments, 128 = num_segments*batch_size. 

How should I handle this problem to save the correct 2048-D tensor per frame?

Kind regards,
Alessandro
